title: Layover ops merchant codes and expense cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for 'layover' style travel days (short hops, long airport waits, unexpected venue changes). Focus is on expense categorization, quick vendor contacts, and immediate-reimbursement tricks so cardholders don't get stuck. Not an official policy — use finance Confluence for final codes, but this is what I actually use in the field.

Top priorities (when in transit):
- keep receipts (photo+email) for every card swipe > $10
- tag expenses immediately in Expensify (mobile) using TRV-INT or TRV-DOM codes below
- if vendor requires PO, escalate to events-ops Slack and grab emergency PO template from Confluence link above

Expense quick-reference (what I usually enter on the fly):
- TRV-INT — international transit (air/train)
- TRV-DOM — domestic transit (uber/taxi/local train)
- LODGING — hotels / short-term stays (attach itemized folio)
- MEALS-PD — meals within per-diem limits (attach receipt)
- MEALS-OUT — client/team meals (list attendees in notes)
- EQUIP-RENT — AV or booth hardware rental (attach vendor invoice)

Receipts and thresholds (finance-friendly):
- always upload photos for any charge > $10
- itemized receipts required for lodging and equipment
- single-meal receipts under $75 are OK with photo; over $75 need manager note
- foreign currency: snap receipt and use Expensify auto-convert; note cash exchanges in comment

Merchant codes I watch for (common false-positives to reclassify):
- AIRLINE/OTA — sometimes shows as "Travel Services" vs vendor name; confirm route/date in notes
- WALLET APPS — e.g., local transit wallets (Tokyo Suica, London Oyster) appear as "Transport Services"; put TRV-DOM
- FOOD COURTS/FOOD HALLS — charge may appear as grocery; if team meal, mark MEALS-OUT and list people

Per-diem quick numbers (use company policy for final):
- US city day: $60 (breakfast $12, lunch $18, dinner $30) — tag MEALS-PD
- EU city day: €55
- APAC: vary (Tokyo/HK ~¥6000/400HKD) — I usually keep to local cap and note conversion

Vendor contacts (first-stop/fast help when layover goes sideways):
- CityLock luggage lockers — Delhi Airport (T3) +91 98765 43210 — quick lockers, accepts cards + cash
- Rent-A-Rig AV — London +44 20 7946 0018 — overnight AV kits, ask for "events emergency kit"
- Rapid SIM kiosk — Changi Terminal 3 +65 6788 4455 — short-term 7/14-day eSIMs and physical SIMs
- Local courier (hotel-to-venue last-mile) — FastShip APAC +65 6222 3344 — use for booth parts under 10kg
- On-call Taxi Desk (SFO) — +1 650 555 0123 — good when rideshares surge

Card and payment notes (personal checklist):
- carry at least two cards: company AMEX + personal backup Visa (last4 check in notes)
- note last4 in expense comment (e.g., AMEX **** 4242) — makes reimbursements faster if finance asks
- if company card declines, put charge on personal and file for immediate reimbursement with manager approval (audio or Slack thread screenshot accepted)

Mobile/Connectivity tips for layovers:
- pre-download vendor invoices (Airbnb/hotel folio) to phone storage
- download PDF copy of Concur/Expensify app receipts export to have offline copies
- keep a screenshot of the emergency PO template (Confluence) in phone photos for quick share

Quick operations checklist (layover day):
- [ ] Photo all receipts as they arrive
- [ ] Create expense in Expensify within 12 hours and tag code
- [ ] Drop short note in Slack #events-ops if any charge > $500 or vendor needs PO
- [ ] If renting gear, confirm pickup/drop times and ask for itemized invoice before leaving vendor site

Common "gotchas" and notes to self:
- airport lounge vendor charges sometimes post with generic "Airport Retail" merchant — ping vendor with flight details and keep boarding pass image
- rental car invoices: get km/miles and fuel details; finance sometimes asks to confirm fuel policy
- booth shipping: small items < 5kg often cheaper to ship with local courier than airport express — call FastShip for quote before accepting hotel shipping price

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for events-ops):
- check whether Expensify should default TRV-INT for all foreign currency charges or if we should classify by merchant type (ask finance lead).
- collect 2 more backup AV vendors in EMEA (Liam to follow up).
- build a one-page PDF with emergency POs and merchant codes for wallets (print to keep in folio) — aim for v1 by 2026-03-15

Attachments I usually include when closing an expense:
- receipt photo(s) (rename with date_vendor_amount.jpg)
- boarding pass image (if flight included)
- vendor invoice (PDF)
- screenshot of Slack approval (if personal card used)

Quick links (copied here so I don't have to look them up on mobile):
- Layover Ops Playbook (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/123456789/Layover+Ops+Playbook
- Events ops Slack: #events-ops
- Finance helpdesk (expenses): finance@redwood.com or Jira TRVL-512

Notes to self (informal):
- remember: photos + immediate tags = fewer post-trip headaches
- if you feel like the charge will trigger an audit (large cash exchange, odd vendor), add a 1–2 line explanation in the expense note right away

End of scratchpad — copy or update as needed per city.
